_note: PROVENANCE for a SYNTHESIZED fixture. No real Visium HD bundle was available in the environment this package was built in, so unlike `spatial-import-visium/tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.json` — which records the licence and source URL of real vendor bytes — this file records where each FORMAT CLAIM the generator encodes comes from. Every byte under `visium-hd-outs/` is in the vendor's own format; none of it is the vendor's own data.
_generator: tests/make_fixture.py — deterministic; `test_fixture_provenance.py` rebuilds into a tmp dir and compares digests, so the committed tree and the generator cannot drift.
_licence: Not applicable: nothing here is redistributed. The fixture is generated by this repository's own committed code.

format_claims.claim: A Visium HD run writes `outs/binned_outputs/square_002um|square_008um|square_016um/`, and each `square_XXXum/` mirrors a full Visium `outs/`.
The Visium HD tissue positions table is PARQUET, not the CSV standard Visium writes.
`scalefactors_json.json` carries `microns_per_pixel` and `bin_size_um` on a Visium HD run, which is why this importer takes the micron scale as STATED rather than deriving it.
The coarser bins nest into the native 2 um grid at 16:1 (8 um) and 64:1 (16 um).
format_claims.encoded_as: the 40x64 / 10x16 / 5x8 lattices, whose row counts are 2560 / 160 / 40

format_claims.claim: The Visium HD capture area is a CONTIGUOUS grid of 2x2 um squares, so a bin's SIDE is also its centre-to-centre PITCH — which is what makes the bin size a usable referent for the scale check.
8 um is 10x's recommended analysis bin, which is the evidence for `DEFAULT_BIN_UM` (not an owner ruling — see DECISIONS.md DEC-1).
format_claims.encoded_as: nothing in the fixture; recorded because the default is read against it

format_claims.claim: The native 2 um bin is too sparse for most analyses, which is why importing it is a deliberate choice rather than the default.

Generated, not measured. `MICRONS_PER_PIXEL`, the lattice size, the tissue ellipse and the count matrix are chosen so the relations the format documents hold exactly; they are not a real run's values.

not_verified.what: what `spot_diameter_fullres` MEANS on a Visium HD bundle, and therefore the value this fixture writes for it (`bin_size_um / microns_per_pixel`)
not_verified.why: No real Visium HD bundle was available, and this repo's only description of the field is 10x's own — "This field is intended for visualization purposes, and can vary for different slide designs, ranging from 60-70 µm" (`docs/research/data-processing/01-file-formats.md:611-612`) — which carries no HD carve-out. The generator derives the value so the fixture's scale numbers cannot contradict each other; that is an internal-consistency choice, not a format fact. The importer derives NOTHING from the field: the scale comes from `microns_per_pixel` and the registration check's referent is the bin lattice pitch. Recorded because #257 is precisely the defect of one reading of this field being taken as true of every bundle.
